title: RPG Maker Web Forum Closure FAQ

posts.body:
About the Closure
Why is the forum shutting down?
As part of upcoming changes to the community management structure, the official RPG Maker forum will transition to a new platform operated by Gotcha Gotcha Games Inc..
This transition is intended to support the continued growth of the RPG Maker community under the new forum, and the current forum will be retired as part of that process.
When will the current forum shut down?
The current forum is scheduled to close on Dec 11th, 2026 (JST).
Please note that certain forum features will be disabled prior to the closure date as part of the transition process.
Will there be an archive or backup of the forum?
No. There are currently no plans to provide a public archive or backup of the current forum once it has been closed.
We encourage users to save any posts, guides, resources, or other content they wish to keep before the forum closure. Content that you would like to continue sharing with the community may be reposted on the new forum.
What happens to the KOMODO Store Purchases and where will we find support for them?
There will be no changes to KOMODO Store purchases or product support as a result of the forum transition.
For assistance with purchases, orders, or product-related inquiries, please continue to use the usual support channels and FAQ resources.
How long will the current forum remain available, and what changes will occur before it closes?
As part of the forum transition, the current forum will gradually phase out its functionality according to the schedule below:
・June 11th, 2026 (JST) – New account registrations will be disabled.
・June 18th, 2026 (JST) – Posting and account activity will be disabled, and the forum will become read-only.
・Dec. 11th, 2026 (JST) – The forum will be permanently closed and will no longer be accessible.
If there is any content you would like to keep, please make sure to save it before the forum closes.
Account & Data
Can I use my current account on the new forum?
No. The new forum is a separate platform, and you will need to create a new account to participate there.
What will happen to my current account information, posts, and forum data?
Your current account information, posts, attachments, and other forum data will not be transferred to the new forum.
As the current forum will be retired, this data will be deleted when the forum closes. If there is any content you would like to keep, please make sure to save it beforehand.
What should I do if there are posts I want to keep?
If there are guides, tutorials, or other posts you would like to preserve, please save them before the current forum closes.
You are also welcome to repost your content on the new forum if you would like to continue sharing it with the community.
Will attachments and images also be deleted?
Yes. Attachments and images are part of the current forum data and will no longer be accessible once the forum is permanently closed.
If there are any files you would like to keep, please download them before the forum closes.
Will private messages also be deleted?
Yes. Private messages will not be transferred to the new forum and will be deleted when the current forum is permanently closed.
If there are any messages you would like to keep, please save them before the forum closes.
RPG Maker & Store Support
Will KOMODO stop supporting RPG Maker products?
No. The forum transition does not affect RPG Maker products.
KOMODO will continue to support store-related services for products purchased through the KOMODO store, including purchases, payments, and product delivery.
Support for individual RPG Maker products is provided by their respective developers and publishers.
Who should users contact for inquiries?
For inquiries regarding the current forum and its closure, please contact KOMODO:
support@rpgmakerweb.com
For inquiries and feedback regarding the new forum, RPG MAKER GUILD / the RPG Maker series visit the link below:
質問
RPGツクールに関する質問を投稿するカテゴリです。投稿時は対象エンジン（MZ/MVなど）と使用言語のタグを付け、状況や再現手順をできるだけ詳しく記載してください。
guild.rpgmakerofficial.com
*Supports multiple languages.
For inquiries related to your RPG MAKER GUILD account, please use the contact form below:
RPG Maker Official | Gotcha Gotcha Games
誰でも簡単に自分だけのゲームが作れる「RPG Maker」オフィシャルサイト。
rpgmakerofficial.com
You can switch between Japanese and English using the JA/EN selector in the upper-right corner of the page.
New Forum
Where is the new official forum?
The new official RPG Maker forum "「RPG MAKER GUILD」" will be operated by Gotcha Gotcha Games.
We encourage community members to visit and participate in the new forum using the link below:
RPG MAKER GUILD
The Official Community for Gotcha Gotcha Games Products
guild.rpgmakerofficial.com
Who will operate the new forum?
Gotcha Gotcha Games Inc. will operate the new official RPG Maker forum.
For inquiries regarding the new forum, please contact Gotcha Gotcha Games using the support resources available on the new forum.
Do I need to create a new account?
Yes. The new forum is a separate platform, and you will need to create a new account to participate.

posts.author: Soul_Narrative_Games
PK8
posts.body:
Self Data Suite creator here.
I would like to balance out much of my criticism by noting how much I appreciate the heads up and the 6-month grace period. However, I'm afraid I'm incapable of properly sandwiching my critique here, so this is all you're going to get in the way of praise. For that, I apologize.
I honestly don't have much of a dog in the fight since I retired/moved on from game dev so long ago. However, I have offline friends who are very much a part of this community.
On behalf of them, I find the decision to move to a brand new platform without offering an easier means to migrate content to be baffling, vaguely reminiscent of a forced forum migration anyone who was around 21 years ago went through (although the circumstances behind that were far more understandable since that was out of everyone's control), and a wholesale spit in the face of the hard work everyone — from the creators that have spent countless sleepless nights bettering their respective talent and producing content to post here all the way down to even the members that show up to ask questions — has put forth here. They are the lifeblood of communities like these. Always have been. Always will be.
While the RM community has always demonstrated incredible resilience in the face of these migrations, it will never excuse the fact that they have always been demoralizing. In the face of this and in the event that any of this is still in yours and the previous management's control, then I would like to do my part in imploring you both to please reconsider this decision to move platforms or at least offer better compromises than a 6-month grace period and a 1-week post limit.
Thank you.
Edit: As an aside to the members, I may be interested in returning to game dev. However, I've lost all ability to write a script. Send me a DM and recommend me a few forums and Discord servers to look into!

Nope. This is actually one of the most outrageous, stupidly braindead things I’ve ever read.
Closing the forums is already bad enough, but
no proper archive?
Seriously? Years and years of community knowledge, plugins, tutorials, bug fixes, troubleshooting threads, scripts, resources, devlogs, conversations, and historical context are just supposed to disappear because people didn’t manually download everything in time?
“If there are any files you would like to keep, please download them before the forum closes.”
LMAOO. What kind of solution is that? How is every user supposed to magically know which files, threads, attachments, screenshots, plugins, or obscure answers they might need in the future? Half the value of a forum is that you find things later when you run into a problem. That’s literally the point.
At the absolute bare minimum, there should be a read-only archive. Communities like this are built over decades, and treating that history like disposable clutter is insulting to everyone who contributed to it.

posts.author: KyluxWolf
posts.body:
Insane. Absolutely insane
I've been relying heavily on this forum for help and inspiration, for plugins, coding tips and to check out the games made by other people. Migrating is already annoying, but I understand that they want to centralize all communications to be in one place that they have full control over.
The decision to not archive ANYTHING? 15 years of support, posts, conversations, just deleted on a whim, forcing US to scrape the forum for resources when there's literally NO WAY of knowing what I will need a year from now?
In an era where archival in general is under attack, with websites like the Internet Archive and the wayback machine always at risk as people in power keep trying to delete history, this has gotta be one of the stupidest, most appalling decisions I've seen to date. And I've been on the internet, I've seen platforms shutting down over and over again, and I've seen them rise again, albeit smaller, thanks to the communities who dedicate precious time and funds to keeping them alive. But I guess I've never seen it happen to a platform that had been around for THIS long, with no migration tools available AT ALL.
You know, I really hoped I could share my game here once it was finished. If this is how little GGG cares about their userbase, I cannot in good faith choose to support any future product or project of theirs. They've lost my trust. In fact, i think they've lost everyone's trust here.

posts.author: matthew30903
posts.body:
I want to say thank you to the staff and community here that have made this a wonderful place.
It is very sad an unfortunate that over a decade of useful information and discussion is about to be lost forever. This move to a new platform will only fracture the English speaking community, break external links to information on this website, and pushes people to closed and siloed platforms.
The RPG Maker Web forums have been RPG Maker's greatest strength in the west compared to other game engines. There is no other game engine with such an active and usable forum.
Modern web forum design favors UI and UX that removes visual complexity at the cost of searchability and actual navigation and the Guild site is no exception. If Guild is the way RPG Maker is going, GGG just destroyed one of their best conversion assets.
In the IndieWeb communities archival has become a major topic of discussion recently due to the massive loss of searchable information due to things being locked to Discord and Reddit. Any community managed by the company that owns the product the community is based around will eventually suffer from some kind of corporate decision making.
The parties involved should try to find a way to either keep these forums open, transfer control of them to the community, or convert the posts to static HTML so the hosting costs of an archive will be negligible.
It is impossible to trust a new web forum when we don't know if what we post there will be taken down when the publisher changes again. I understand there are legal difficulties and GGG likely wants control over the community, but this is not the way to do it. These forums are what made the western audience for RPG Maker so vibrant and is a shining example of what forums could be in the modern age, it is sad to see them go.

posts.author: Soryuju
posts.body:
I haven't posted here since 2020 and was only really active on the forums for a couple of years, but I just wanted to make one final visit and give my thanks to the community. Y'all are amazing, and I probably would have quit RPG Maker within weeks of starting if it weren't for the abundance of design advice, technical support, resources, and general encouragement from the passionate folks here. Sometimes when I was in a slump, I would just browse through the project threads to see all of the wonderful games people were making, and it would give me the second wind I needed.
I'll miss this place, and I'm furious at the disrespect that GGG has shown to the community with this abrupt closure. The good people who have spent years or even decades contributing to this forum are the reason RPG Maker is one of the most accessible engines currently on the market, and to cut the community off at the knees like this speaks volumes about how little GGG appreciates those efforts. You deserved better.
Anyways, I hope y'all succeed in preserving this place and finding a lovely new home. I'll probably at least end up lurking around wherever everyone ends up, and who knows, maybe someday I'll actually post a game. If I do, I'll owe it all to you. So one last time: thank you for everything.

I'm also curious how the EULA change affects tilesets created from edited RTP. Would those be okay to use in other engines (as long as you own the proper RPG Maker engine) or is it still a case-by-case basis depending on the creator?
Click to expand...
The "Makes Series Only" designation comes from the creators themselves. I think it was Finalbossblues that said the RPG Maker only versions of his assets were cheaper than his engine agnostic versions because of the restriction. You could ask the creator specifically for permission.
As for RTP edits, depends on the terms of use of the editor/creator. Most of them just specify you have to own the RPG Maker the base asset came from.
Magenta-Fantasies said:
As someone who switched to Unity, from what I've heard, the lack of success for RPG Maker Unite was a combination of lack of features, especially for the $100 price tag, long loading times, poor performance and many bugs.
Click to expand...
Most of the bugs and load times have been fixed. Unite gets more updates than MZ and is still getting updates last I checked. It also regularly goes on sale for $25, less than MZ on sale and has been as cheap as $10 during the Beyond Expectations Humble Bundle sale. Users still haven't adopted it. I think it's the lack of features because 3rd party support is non-existent, and GGG hasn't provided enough first party features.
